newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Congress approves war bonds.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Congress approves war bonds.

text.p: Congress has approved legislation requiring wealthy Colombians to buy war bonds next year to help finance the long-running battle with leftist guerrillas.

The legislation proposed by President Ernesto Samper in September was approved late on Tuesday by the lower house of Congress following its passage in the Senate last week. It requires individuals or businesses with a net worth of more than $150,000 at the close of 1996 to invest 0.5 percent of their total assets in the five-year bonds.

The bonds will carry annual interest equal to 80 percent of the official inflation rate in 1996, which is expected to top 21 percent. Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo told reporters the government expected to raise about $420 million through the sale of the bonds, although senior military officials have said they hoped the extraordinary measure would boost military spending by as much as $600 million in 1997.
Apart from the purchase of war materiel, the Defence Ministry has said it plans to use the additional funds to add at least 7,600 members to Colombia's 120,000-strong military.

Estimates of the number of guerrillas across Colombia vary widely. Diplomats say the two largest and oldest rebel armies, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) and National Liberation Army (ELN), are believed to total no more than about 15,000.

Both groups have grown rich through a nationwide campaign of kidnappings and extortion, however, and the military has accused the FARC of growing involvement in Colombia's lucrative drug trade. Western experts say the FARC, particularly, poses more of a threat today than at any time since its founding as a pro-Soviet Marxist group in 1964.
